15 days until the August SAT.

Circle questions look brutal in general form. Desmos will graph that form exactly as the SAT prints it — so instead of completing the square, you draw the circle and read what you need off the grid.

Save this one — it's the whole topic in one place. Seva's practice tests have the same calculator built in, so you can drill these until they're reflex. Free trial — link in bio.

slides.badge: Graph general form, read the rest off the grid

slides.title: Paste general form in — it just draws it
slides.tip: Desmos won't hand you the centre, but it will graph the equation without any conversion first.

slides.title: Read them off the gridlines
slides.tip: The middle sits at (-4, 5) and it's 6 squares to the edge, so r = 6. Counting beats algebra.

slides.title: Prove your completed square is right
slides.tip: Graph your standard form on top. If the dashed circle lands exactly on the solid one, you did it correctly.

slides.title: Where a line cuts the circle
slides.tip: Graph both and read the crossings: (-4, -3) and (3, 4). No substitution, no messy quadratic.
